headline: Protein and nucleic acid design tools benchmarked for fitness and specificity
label: Computational Sequence Design Models
summary: Sequence design pipelines are now evaluated at increasing mutational distance and across nucleic acid and RNA codon targets.
synthesis: The preprints share a sequence-design framing in which generative models or language-model scores propose or rank variants. DeePEn tests fitness prediction at increasing mutational distance across four DMS datasets. A separate benchmark finds language models bias against altered-specificity variants, and weighted score differences enrich for them. HalluDesign-NA couples NA-MPNN optimization with AlphaFold3 refinement for nucleic acids. An AAV study pairs deep sequencing with protein language models to map viable VR-VIII insertions. DGRec hypermutagenesis design and RNARL multi-objective codon design, the latter covering sequences over 3,900 nt, extend the approach to recombination templates and RNA. The new element is evaluation beyond single-point fitness, toward specificity, nucleic acid, and long-RNA targets.
